```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(tmap)

# Read in geodatabase of EJScreen data at the Census Block Group level
ejscreen <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "ejscreen","EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb")) 

# Filter to California
california <- ejscreen %>%
  dplyr::filter(ST_ABBREV == "CA") 

# Filter to San Joaquin County
san_joaquin <- ejscreen %>%
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME %in% c("San Joaquin County"))

# Find the average values for all variables within counties
california_counties <- aggregate(california, by = list(california$CNTY_NAME), FUN = mean)
```

```{r}
# Plot percentile of wastewater discharge
sj_waterdischarge <-tm_shape(san_joaquin)+  # Define the spacial object to plot 
  tm_title('Waterwater Discharge in San Joaquin County (2023)')+
  tm_polygons(fill= 'P_PWDIS', fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Toxicity-weighted concentration / km"))+ 
  tm_add_legend(type = "line", col = "white") +
  tm_layout(bg.color = "white")+
  tm_style("white") +
  tm_compass() +
  tm_scalebar() 
```
```{r}
# Plot EJScreen Supplemental Demographic Index
# Supplemental Demographic Index is based on the average of two demographic indicators; Percent Low-Income and Percent Minority.
sj_demographic <- tm_shape(san_joaquin)+ # Define the spacial object to plot 
    tm_polygons(fill= 'P_DEMOGIDX_2', fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Average of percent
low income and percent people of color")) +
    tm_title('EJ Demographic Index in San Joaquin County (2023)')+
    tm_add_legend(type = "line", col = "white") +
    tm_layout(bg.color = "white")+
    tm_style("beaver") +
    tm_compass(type ="arrow") +
    tm_scalebar() #percentile of wastewater discharge
```

```{r}
# Arrange maps in a grid
tmap_arrange(sj_waterdischarge, sj_demographic)
```

## Mapping summary: 


In San Joaquin County, unsafe water quality poses a major public health threat, particularly for communities identified by EJScreen’s demographic indicators. Water contamination and toxicity have been linked to agricultural and industrial activity, but the full scope of exposure is difficult to measure because much of the available data does not account for people who travel through, recreate in, or work near contaminated water.

The map on the left (Wastewater Discharge in San Joaquin County, 2023) shows wastewater discharge from permitted facilities, measured as toxicity-weighted concentration divided by distance in meters. The map on the right (EJ Demographic Index in San Joaquin County, 2023) shows a demographic index based on percent low-income and percent people of color. In the western part of the county, areas with high wastewater toxicity substantially overlap with areas scoring high on the demographic index.
